title: Registering Models with the Admin
description: Make your models appear in the admin and customize their display.

slides.title: Basic Registration
slides.content: In your app’s `admin.py`, import your model and register it with the admin site.
slides.codeSnippet:
from django.contrib import admin
from .models import Post

admin.site.register(Post)

slides.title: What You Get Immediately 🎁
slides.content:
After registration, you’ll see a list view of all `Post` objects with a link to add or change them. Clicking an item opens a detailed edit form with fields generated from the model.

Django automatically:
- Validates input based on model constraints.
- Provides a search box (if you add `search_fields`).
- Supports pagination and filtering (if you add `list_filter`).

quizData.question: Where should you place the code to register a model with the admin?
quizData.explanation: Admin registrations belong in `admin.py` inside your app.

slides.title: Using a ModelAdmin Class
slides.content: For more control, create a `ModelAdmin` subclass and register it with the model.
slides.codeSnippet:
from django.contrib import admin
from .models import Post

class PostAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin):
    list_display = ('title', 'author', 'published_date')
    search_fields = ('title', 'content')

admin.site.register(Post, PostAdmin)

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Use `@admin.register` decorator

A cleaner way:
```python
@admin.register(Post)
class PostAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin):
    list_display = ('title', 'author')
```
